Compute Gaussian Process Log-Likelihood (with Optional Quadratic Mean)

compute_like.Rd

Evaluate the (negative) log-likelihood of observed data under a Gaussian Process model, optionally including a linear-plus-quadratic mean function.

Usage

compute_like(
  length_scale,
  x,
  y,
  signal_var,
  noise_var,
  D,
  quad = FALSE,
  nu = Inf
)

Arguments

length_scale

Positive numeric scalar or vector of length-scales for each dimension.

x

Numeric vector or matrix of training inputs (rows = observations).

y

Numeric vector of training responses.

signal_var

Positive numeric scalar specifying the GP signal variance (\(\sigma^2\)).

noise_var

Positive numeric scalar specifying observation noise variance.

D

Integer. Dimensionality of the input space (number of columns in x).

quad

Logical; if FALSE (default), assume zero-mean GP. If TRUE, include a mean function \(\beta_0 + x^\top \beta_1 + (x \otimes x)^\top \beta_2\).

nu

Positive numeric specifying the smoothness parameter for the Matérn kernel. Defaults to Inf, selecting the Squared Exponential kernel.

Value

A numeric scalar giving the negative log-likelihood (up to an additive constant). Extremely large values (\(10^{20}\)) are returned if the computation produces NaN, NA, or infinite results.

Details

Zero-mean GP (quad = FALSE):

  1. Build covariance \(C = K_{xx} + \sigma_n^2 I\) via cov_generator.

  2. Compute Cholesky factor \(L L^T = C\).

  3. Log-determinant: \(\log\det(C) = 2\sum\log(\mathrm{diag}(L))\).

  4. Precision \(Q = C^{-1} = \texttt{chol2inv}(L)\). .

  5. Negative log-likelihood: $$\frac{1}{2}\,y^T Q\,y \;-\; \log\det(Q) \;-\;\sum \log\bigl[\text{LogNormal}(\texttt{length_scale}\mid \texttt{prior_l})\bigr]$$

GP with quadratic mean (quad = TRUE):

  1. Construct design matrix \(X = [1,\,x,\,\mathrm{unique}(x \otimes x)]\).

  2. Build \(C = K_{xx} + \sigma^2_n I\) and its precision \(Q\).

  3. Form marginal precision \(S = X^\top Q X\) and invert via Cholesky.

  4. Compute two quadratic terms: \(\tfrac12\,y^\top Q\,y\) and \(\tfrac12\,y^\top Q X S^{-1} X^\top Q\,y\).

  5. Combine with log-determinants of \(Q\) and \(S^{-1}\) and the log-prior to yield the final negative log-likelihood.

Examples

# Zero-mean SE kernel likelihood (Not run)
# x <- matrix(seq(0,1,length.out=5), ncol=1)
# y <- sin(2*pi*x)
# like0 <- compute_like(length_scale = 0.2,
#                        x = x, y = y,
#                        signal_var = 1,
#                        noise_var  = 1e-3,
#                        D = 1,
#                        prior_l_mean = 0,
#                        prior_l_sd   = 1,
#                        quad = FALSE,
#                        nu   = Inf)

# GP with quadratic mean
# like2 <- compute_like(length_scale = 0.3,
#                       x = x, y = y,
#                        signal_var = 1,
#                        noise_var  = 1e-3,
#                        D = 1,
#                        prior_l_mean = 0,
#                        prior_l_sd   = 1,
#                        quad = TRUE,
#                        nu   = Inf)
